solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Son blocks unwanted email then second starts

indicators.note: the son blocks the email by standing in the middle of it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: spam is junk email

explanation.surface: A boy filters out his junk mail, and then another thing kicks off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocks' puts S inside SPAM to give SPASM, then the second S is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasms are sudden involuntary jerks, so they can be called starts, as in waking with a start.

clue.text: John Lennon for one left melody first

indicators.note: melody comes first, so its piece is placed ahead of the word for left

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody
port is the nautical word for the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A Beatle is described as having left, with a tune leading the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool's airport is named Liverpool John Lennon Airport, so the Beatle's name stands for the place, not the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool John Lennon Airport is an example of an air terminal named after a famous person.

clue.text: Bald head can be severe condition

parts.note: stark can mean bare or plain, as bald does
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A man going bald worries it may be a serious medical problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is not the top of the bald man's skull but a geographical headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Starkness is the quality of being harsh and severe, so it describes a severe state of things.

clue.text: Demonstration rearranged by university at the designated place

indicators.note: the protest word has its letters moved round from one end to the other, which is the rearrangement

parts.note: a sit-in is a form of protest demonstration

explanation.surface: A student protest is reorganised by the college authorities in the proper location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demonstration rearranged' looks like an anagram of the clue word, but it is the protest word with its two halves swapped round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in the original or appointed position, in its proper place.

clue.text: Sally and Harry originally are small parts

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letters of the two names, where each begins

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Sally and Harry seem to be cast as minor characters in a film or play.
explanation.walkthrough: The names recall the film When Harry Met Sally, but only their initial letters S and H are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Shares are portions or allotted parts of something divided between people.

clue.text: Did hero's treatment get more slapdash?

indicators.note: giving the letters a treatment means working them over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the hero's handling of things got sloppier.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of DID HEROS are rearranged; the possessive apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddier means of poorer quality or more carelessly done, the comparative of a synonym for slapdash.

clue.text: Decline not in short representative

parts.note: to age is to decline or grow older and weaker
n't is the shortened, contracted form of not

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to take part in a briefly-stated role as delegate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like refuse, but here it means to deteriorate with age.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acts on behalf of someone else, so is their representative.

clue.text: Sties are blots on the landscape

definitions.meaning: styes, also spelt sties, are inflamed swellings on the eyelid, so they are sore spots on eyes
ugly buildings or sights that spoil a view

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sties' suggests pigsties, which suit the landscape picture, but here it is the eyelid infection.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is an ugly thing that spoils a view, a blot on the landscape.

clue.text: Virgin Trains' pie not a crumble

indicators.note: not says the letters of the word a are absent from the mix
to crumble is to break into pieces, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A rail operator's pie is praised for not falling to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of TRAINS PIE, remove an A, and rearrange what remains. Virgin Trains was a British rail operator, which makes 'Virgin' look like a company name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pristine means untouched and unspoiled, as something virgin is.

clue.text: Doctor Who always just the same

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of the next word are altered in order

parts.note: ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: The TV time traveller is said to be forever unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Who' reads as the TV show, but 'Doctor' is the anagram signal acting on WHO.
explanation.definitionFit: However and just the same both mean nevertheless, introducing a contrast.

clue.text: Marvellous making use of change in purse

indicators.note: a change in the word means its letters are rearranged, while the surface suggests coins in a purse

explanation.surface: It is wonderful to use the coins in one's purse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' suggests loose coins, but here it signals rearranging the letters of PURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is an informal synonym for marvellous or excellent.

clue.text: Chase after stinkers — a kind of fungus

indicators.note: chase comes after stinkers, so its piece follows in the answer

parts.note: toads are contemptible people, stinkers
to chase or tool metal or leather is to decorate it with engraved patterns

explanation.surface: Someone pursues a pack of rotters, and then a type of fungus appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chase' is not pursue but the craftsman's sense of engraving metal, which tool shares.
explanation.definitionFit: A toadstool is an umbrella-shaped fungus, often poisonous, a kind of mushroom.

clue.text: Settle old vacant plot

indicators.note: a vacant word has its middle emptied, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to settle an old empty piece of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacant plot' looks like empty land, but it means PLOT with its insides removed, leaving PT.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to choose, and to settle on something is to make that choice.

clue.text: Executed last of tasks before time's called

indicators.note: the letter from tasks comes before the rest in the answer
last of picks the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: rung up means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: The last job is finished before closing time is announced in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time's called' sounds like the landlord calling time in a British pub, but it is T plus RUNG UP, with 's as is.
explanation.definitionFit: Strung up means hanged, put to death by hanging, so executed.

clue.text: Shun champ found with illegal tablets

parts.note: Es are ecstasy tablets, an illegal drug
to champ is to chew noisily

explanation.surface: A sporting champion is caught with banned pills and is shunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champ' reads as a champion, but it is the verb meaning to munch.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to avoid or abstain from it deliberately.

clue.text: Latest worry involving work pressure

indicators.note: involving means the word for worry wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: stress is worry or strain
OP is short for opus, a musical work
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: The newest anxiety concerns stress at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: Stop press is a newspaper column for news added at the last minute, which makes 'Latest' a fair definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The stop-press column carries late news inserted after printing began, the latest stories.

clue.text: 'Doris' (she writes) below book dedication

indicators.note: in a down answer the writer's name is placed below the letter for book

parts.note: Doris Lessing was a Nobel prize-winning novelist, the woman who writes

explanation.surface: A novelist's name appears under the title in a book's dedication page.
explanation.walkthrough: Doris Lessing, the Nobel-winning novelist, supplies her surname; '(she writes)' tells you Doris is a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A blessing or consecration ceremony is a dedication, setting something apart as holy.

clue.text: Health resort in southern Pennsylvania

parts.note: PA is the US postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania

explanation.surface: A wellness retreat located in the south of an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a place with mineral springs or treatments visited for health.

clue.text: Architectural feature mapped — I'm enthralled somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A traveller is captivated by a building feature found on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: A pediment is the triangular gable over a classical portico, a feature of buildings.

clue.text: Banks of earth eroded making work

indicators.note: the banks of a word are its edges, its outermost letters
eroded says those edges are worn away, leaving only the centre

explanation.surface: Erosion of earth embankments makes the ground move.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E and H, the outer letters of EARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A work of art, as in a gallery's works, is a piece of creative output.

clue.text: Pass English courses with low grade

parts.note: laps are circuits or courses of a track
E is a low exam grade

explanation.surface: A student scrapes through English classes with a poor mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' suggests school classes, but here it means laps of a track.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse or pass, meaning go by.

clue.text: Briton's oddly brief history

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A British person's quirky short biography.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bio is an informal word for a short biography, a person's brief life history.

clue.text: Doubting Thomas, Charlie and Penny are among names revived

indicators.note: revived suggests bringing back to life in a new form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: to cite is to name or mention
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned names like Charlie and Penny are coming back, though one person doubts it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie and Penny' look like revived baby names, but they give C and P, which mix with CITES; 'are among' just links them.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubting Thomas is a person who refuses to believe without proof, a doubter.

clue.text: Dreadfully sick after one mushroom — they can be deadly in the wrong hands

definitions.text: they can be deadly in the wrong hands

indicators.note: the mixed word comes after the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a cep is a kind of edible mushroom, the porcini

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests the word is in a terrible state, so its letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone falls terribly ill after eating a mushroom, which can be fatal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadfully' turns SICK into ICKS. The mushroom picture suggests poisoning, but the deadly things are climbers' tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice picks are pointed tools that could serve as murder weapons if misused.

clue.text: Mini Minors may be parked here?

definitions.text: Mini Minors may be parked here?

parts.words: Mini Minors may be parked here?
parts.note: Mini Minor was a classic British small car, but here the words mean tiny children left in a day nursery

explanation.walkthrough: The Morris Mini Minor was a small British car of the 1960s, so 'parked' suggests a car park.
explanation.definitionFit: A creche is a nursery where young children are looked after while parents are busy.

clue.text: Depressed with range of knowledge shown by tabloid

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
ken is one's range of knowledge, as in beyond my ken

explanation.surface: Someone is gloomy about how little the popular press seems to know.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depressed' looks like gloomy, but it is the physical sense of sunk down. The Sun is a British tabloid paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sunken has been pressed down below the surrounding level, as with depressed ground.

clue.text: Austria and Thailand once popular — or most of Turkey

parts.note: A is the international vehicle code for Austria
Siam was the former name of Thailand
in means popular or fashionable
taken as written

explanation.surface: A travel list of formerly fashionable destinations, ending with Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatolia, the peninsula forming the bulk of modern Turkey, was historically called by this name.

clue.text: Savour run by Farah back among amateurs

indicators.note: among says the other pieces sit inside the pair of letters for amateurs

parts.note: A is short for amateur, so two of them are AA
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: back says the runner's first name is read backwards

parts.note: Mo Farah is the British Olympic distance runner

explanation.surface: A runner's performance is enjoyed when he returns to amateur athletics.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo Farah is a British long-distance runner, so 'run by Farah' fits the athletics picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Savour as a noun means a characteristic smell or taste, an aroma.

clue.text: What Edith Piaf regretted about piano's age

indicators.note: about means the French word wraps around the musical letter

parts.note: Piaf sang Non, je ne regrette rien, so she regretted nothing, in French rien
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A singer's regrets turn on how old her piano is.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith Piaf's famous song says she regrets nothing, 'rien'. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To age, as cheese or wine does, is to mature, ripening with time.

clue.text: Fellow whose wife is sadly late

definitions.text: Fellow whose wife is sadly late

parts.words: Fellow whose wife is sadly late
parts.note: late here means dead, not behind time, so the man has lost his spouse

explanation.walkthrough: 'late' suggests a wife who is unpunctual, but it means deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: A man whose spouse has died and who has not remarried is so called.

clue.text: Modest about one's discipline

indicators.note: about means the word for modest goes around the other piece

parts.note: chaste means pure and modest
one is I, and one's gives I plus S

explanation.surface: A modest person reflects on their own self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discipline' is a verb here, meaning to punish.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise someone is to punish or rebuke them, to discipline them.

clue.text: Horrified husband's gripped by stove's temperature

indicators.note: gripped by means the husband's letter is held inside the stove word

parts.note: an Aga is a British range cooker, a heavy stove

explanation.surface: A husband is shocked to be held fast by the heat of the cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a British brand of cast-iron range cooker; the 's on husband's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with horror or shock, horrified.
